entities.summary:
Ibar mac Lugna, known as Ibar of Beggerin or Iberius, was an early Irish saint and bishop who played a pivotal role in the island's early Christianization. Born around 450 CE, Ibar was said to have been one of the 'Quattuor sanctissimi Episcopi,' a group of four bishops who preceded Saint Patrick in Ireland. His feast day is celebrated on April 23, and he is the patron saint of Beggerin Island.

    Ibar's significance extends beyond his role as a bishop, as he is believed to have been a key figure in the conversion of the Irish people to Christianity. His legacy has endured for centuries, with his feast day remaining an important part of Irish cultural heritage. The exact circumstances of Ibar's life and death are not well-documented, but his impact on Irish history is undeniable.

    The legacy of Ibar of Beggerin can be seen in the many churches and monasteries that bear his name throughout Ireland. His feast day is still celebrated with great fervor, and his image appears on various Irish coins and artwork.

    In the 7th century, Ibar's relics were believed to have been transported to the monastery of Kells, where they remain to this day. This transfer of relics had a profound impact on the religious and cultural landscape of Ireland, cementing Ibar's status as a revered figure in Irish Christianity.
